attempts.summary: Configured node1 and node2 (SONiC-VS routers) to exchange each other's private-network prefixes (192.168.10.0/24 behind node1↔node3, 192.168.20.0/24 behind node2↔node4) via iBGP over the eth1 transit link (172.20.1.0/31), extending SONiC's existing AS 65100 FRR instance rather than entering static routes. node3/node4 got static host routes to their own gateway only (normal leaf-host config, not the protocol under test). Verified end-to-end node3↔node4 reachability over the private path, then performed the mandatory one-at-a-time restart protocol on all 4 nodes with boot-id proof and post-restart re-verification of BGP sessions, kernel routes, and connectivity. Discovered and fixed a persistence gap: SONiC's bgp container regenerates FRR config from configdb templates on boot, silently dropping manually-added vtysh neighbors — added a systemd oneshot (apply-transit-bgp.service) on node1/node2 that reapplies the iBGP neighbor/network config once bgpd is ready on every boot; interface IPs and forwarding sysctls were persisted via /etc/network/interfaces.d/ and /etc/sysctl.d/, and node3/node4's private IP+route via NetworkManager connection profiles.
